what: “In the beginning”: heavens and earth created
note: Undated. The universe exists before the first creative day begins. (Genesis 1:1)
Six long epochs: light, expanse, land and vegetation, luminaries discernible, sea and sky creatures, land animals and mankind.
Dust and breath. Bible chronology’s first countable anchor. (Genesis 2:7)

what: The garden, the command, the first marriage
note: Work and boundaries before sin; Eve built from Adam’s side; Genesis 2:24 stated for all time.
Blessed and made sacred; per Hebrews 4, still ongoing in the first century. (Genesis 2:2, 3)
“You certainly will not die.” Jehovah’s truthfulness and way of ruling are challenged before all creation. (Genesis 3:1-6)
Enmity, two seeds, a struck heel, a crushed head. The scarlet thread begins; every covenant to come will carry it. Status: unfolding.

what: Cherubs guard the way east of Eden
note: Access to the tree of life barred, until Revelation 22 reopens it. Humanity’s history outside the garden begins. (Genesis 3:22-24)
The first offerings in history. Jehovah weighs the giver with the gift; Hebrews 11:4 names the difference: faith.
Abel’s blood cries out from the ground; Cain departs to Nod. The two lines of Genesis 3:15 are now visible in history.
“Another offspring in place of Abel.” Genesis 5:3 gives the chronology its second anchor; the begat-chain begins.
365 years, then “God took him”: spared death’s pangs in a hostile age. His prophecy of judgment is preserved in Jude 14, 15.
“Dust you will return,” kept. Within one thousand-year “day” by the scale of 2 Peter 3:8, the sentence of Eden is fully executed.
The first of the seed line born after Adam’s death. His father names him in hope of comfort from the cursed ground. (Genesis 5:29)
Sons of God take human wives; their hybrid sons fill the earth with violence. Peter and Jude date the angels’ fall to Noah’s day.
“My spirit will not tolerate man indefinitely.” Judgment is dated for the first time; Noah is 480, and his sons are not yet born. (Genesis 6:3)
“I am establishing my covenant with you”: the word covenant enters Scripture. Noah builds, and preaches, for the better part of a century.
Month 2, day 17 of Noah’s 600th year: the springs burst, the floodgates open, and Jehovah shuts the door. Both countdowns expire on schedule.

what: The ark rests on the mountains of Ararat
note: Five months to the day from the rain’s beginning. The raven, the dove, and the olive leaf follow.

what: “Go out of the ark” · the first altar
note: After 370 days aboard, Noah’s first act is worship, and heaven answers with the oath of the seasons. (Genesis 8:20-22)
Everlasting, unconditional, made with every living creature: never again a deluge to ruin the earth. The sign is set where God’s own eyes will see it. (Genesis 9:13-16)
Cursed be Canaan; praised be Jehovah, the God of Shem. The seed line narrows to one of three brothers. (Genesis 9:20-27)
Two years before the birth of Abraham. The chain of living memory from Eden to the man of the promise has no real gap: Shem outlives into Abraham’s day.
The Table of Nations’ timestamp. Babel falls within his days, while the Flood’s survivors still lived. (Genesis 10:25)

what: Babel: the confusion and the scattering
note: One faculty touched, no lives recorded taken, and the mandate to fill the earth fulfills itself through the dispersal built against. (Genesis 11:1-9)
In the civilization of Shinar, the man of the promise arrives. Season Two of this Library begins with him.
The Abrahamic covenant takes effect, and the 430-year count to the Exodus begins, “on this very day.” (Genesis 12:4; Exodus 12:41)

what: Shechem: Jehovah appears; the first altar
note: “To your offspring I am going to give this land.” Tents and altars: the pattern of the promise-holder’s whole life. (Genesis 12:7)

what: Famine, Egypt, and the guarded promise
note: The promise-bearer improvises in fear; the Promise-Maker guards the promise anyway. Abram returns wealthy and intact. (Genesis 12:10-20)
In the wilderness of Sinai, to a nation newly freed from Egypt: the account’s first audience.
